requirement.description: A dealer is a person or firm carrying on the business of buying, selling, supplying or distributing packaged commodities, directly or otherwise, for consideration; the definition includes a commission agent acting for a principal, subject to the manufacturer-related exclusion stated in the rule.

requirement.description: An industrial consumer is a consumer purchasing packaged commodities directly from a manufacturer, importer or wholesale dealer for use by the industry, with the package bearing the prescribed “not for retail sale” treatment.

applicability.scope: Interpretation of LMPC terminology

requirement.description: An institutional consumer is an institution purchasing packaged commodities directly from a manufacturer, importer or wholesale dealer for institutional use and not for commercial or trade purposes, with the prescribed “not for retail sale” treatment.

requirement.description: The package must state the month and year in which the commodity was manufactured, subject to the specified exceptions and later product-specific provisos.

source.amendment: G.S.R. 779(E), 02-11-2021; later product-specific provisos are recorded separately

requirement.description: For electronic products, spare parts and accessories, the amended regime permits the month/year information to be supplied in the manner provided by the relevant proviso, including the QR-code mechanism where applicable.
Where applicable, the package must carry the prescribed best-before or use-by information.

The package must state the retail sale price in the prescribed manner, including the maximum- retail-price presentation in Indian currency, inclusive of all taxes, subject to the rule's sectoral-law and package exceptions.
Where dimensions of the commodity are relevant, the package must state the dimensions; where pieces differ, the dimensions of each different piece must be stated.
For covered electronic products, specified size/dimension information may be supplied through the permitted QR-code mechanism.
The package must also carry any other matter that the Rules specifically require, including requirements arising under later sub-rules/provisos.
Every package must provide the prescribed name/address/contact information of the person or office that can be contacted for consumer complaints.
For covered electronic products, specified consumer-care contact information may be handled through the continuing QR-code mechanism while retaining the particulars required directly on the package.

Individual stickers cannot ordinarily be used to alter or make a declaration required by the Rules. A lower revised MRP sticker is permitted subject to the stated condition that it must not cover the original MRP declaration.
Stickers may be used for declarations that are not declarations required to be made under the Rules.
The package may carry optional barcode, GTIN, QR/e-code and permitted government-scheme information in accordance with the provision.

Where a commodity consists of components packed in two or more units and sold as one commodity, the required declaration must appear on the main package with the prescribed information about accompanying packages; where components are sold as spare parts, declarations must be given on each package.

Unused packaging material/wrappers could be used during the specified transitional period after the permitted corrections by stamping, sticker or online printing. The operative historical period ended on 31 March 2012.

The 2015 amendment inserted this provision as part of the Rule 6 declaration framework; its operative requirements must be selected according to the applicable version and product category.
An e-commerce entity must ensure that the mandatory declarations required by Rule 6 are displayed on the electronic network used for e-commerce, subject to the exceptions and conditions in the rule.
From 1 July 2026, every e-commerce entity selling imported products must provide product listings of those imported products in a searchable and sortable filter specifying the country of origin.

From 1 July 2027, the second 2026 amendment substitutes the above wording so that every e-commerce entity offering an imported product for sale must ensure the product listing contains a searchable and sortable filter specifying the country of origin.

requirement.description: The unit-sale-price declaration is not required for the package categories specifically excluded by the proviso, including combination, group and multi-piece packages.
For a package having a capacity of 10 cubic centimetres or less, the principal display panel may be a firmly affixed card or tape carrying the required information.
The height of any numeral and letter in the declaration required under these rules shall be as per Table-I. Table-II was omitted by G.S.R. 629(E).
For packages containing medical devices, the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 apply for the height of numerals where the inserted proviso is applicable.
The width of a letter or numeral shall not be less than one-third of its height, except for numeral 1 and letters i, I and l.
For packages containing medical devices, the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 govern the applicable height/width declaration dimensions under the inserted proviso.
Rule 7(4) determines the area of the principal display panel after the stated exclusions, using clauses (a) to (c).
For a rectangular package where one entire side can properly be considered the principal display panel side, the area is height multiplied by width of that side.

title: Cylindrical or nearly cylindrical PDP area

requirement.description: For a cylindrical or nearly cylindrical package, the principal display panel area is 40 per cent of height multiplied by circumference.
For any other shaped package, the principal display panel area is 40 per cent of total surface area or an area considered to be a principal display panel.

Except for the size of numbers and letters used for net weight, retail sale price, expiry/best- before/use-by date and consumer-care details, sub-rules (1) to (4) do not apply where the same information is required by or under another law.

Every declaration required by the Rules must appear on the principal display panel. The area surrounding the quantity declaration must remain free of printed information by the minimum vertical and horizontal clear-space distances specified.

For returnable bottles used for soft drinks, ready-to-serve fruit beverages or similar products, the MRP may be shown on the crown cap, the bottle, or both; “MRP Rs....” is sufficient in the permitted case.
Every required package declaration must be legible and prominent.
Information blown, formed or moulded on glass or plastic need not be presented in a contrasting colour.
Structured representation of Handwritten/hand-script declarations.

title: Contrasting colour for MRP and quantity

requirement.description: Numerals for retail sale price and net quantity must be printed, painted or inscribed in a colour that contrasts conspicuously with the label background.
Declarations must not be made in a manner that requires them to be read through the liquid commodity contained in the package.

Where a package has an outside container or wrapper, that outer layer must also carry the required declarations unless it is transparent and the declarations on the inner package are easily readable through it.
Structured representation of Permitted languages.

Every package kept, offered, exposed or sold must conspicuously bear the manufacturer’s complete name and address, and where applicable the packer and importer details. Small packages have the permitted mark/inscription alternative, and imported goods packed in India have the additional principal-display-panel requirement.

Complete address includes the prescribed postal/location information sufficient for a consumer to identify and locate the manufacturer, packer or importer. The wording was updated by the 2015 amendment to reflect the registered company/firm address formulation.
The name used must be the actual corporate name or, where the entity is not incorporated, the name under which the business is conducted in India.
Where significant variation can occur because of environmental or other conditions, the quantity declaration may be qualified by “when packed” for commodities specified in the Third Schedule.
When declaring net quantity, the weight of wrappers and materials other than the commodity itself must be excluded.

If the commodity is not likely to vary in weight/measure because of environmental conditions, the declared quantity must correspond to what the consumer will receive and must not be qualified by “when packed” or similar words.

Where variation is likely but negligible, the declaration must account for the variation so that the consumer receives not less than the declared quantity; “when packed” or similar qualification is not permitted.
Quantity must be expressed in the unit of weight, measure, number or permitted combination that gives the consumer accurate and adequate information about the quantity.

title: Mass for solid/semi-solid/viscous mixtures

requirement.description: Except for Fourth Schedule cases, solid, semi-solid, viscous and solid-liquid mixture commodities are declared by mass.

requirement.description: Commodities sold by linear measure are declared by length.
Commodities sold by area measure are declared by area.
Liquid commodities or commodities sold by cubic measure are declared by volume.
Commodities sold by number are declared by number.
Where quantity is declared by mass, the manufacturer, importer or packer may additionally state the number of commodities in the package.
Where weight, measure or number alone is insufficient to give the consumer full information, the declaration must also state dimensions, number, or both, as necessary.
Any additional information necessary to communicate relevant facts about the commodity must appear on the same panel as the other required information.

The quantity declaration must not use words or expressions that create an exaggerated, misleading or inadequate impression about quantity, including expressions such as minimum, not less than, average, about or approximately.

For packages of capacity 5 cubic centimetres or less, the quantity declaration is made on a tag, card, tape or similar device attached so it cannot be removed without opening the container, with identification of the manufacturer/packer.
No unit system other than the International System of Units may be used for furnishing package net quantity.
Units of weight, measure or number must be specified according to the unit rules in sub-rules (2) and (3).
The unit of weight is gram.
The unit of length is centimetre.
The unit of area is square decimetre.
The unit of volume is cubic centimetre.
The unit of volume is cubic centimetre.
The unit of volume is millilitre.

requirement.description: Every individual, firm, Hindu undivided family, society, company or corporation that pre-packs or imports a commodity for sale/distribution/delivery must apply to the Director/Controller with the prescribed fee and within the prescribed 90-day period.
The registration application must state the applicant’s name.
The application must state the complete address of the premises where pre-packing or import is carried out.
The application must state the commodity or commodities pre-packed or imported.
From 29 May 2026, the registration particulars include the name of the Director of the company responsible for violations under the Act and Rules.
Complete address has the meaning assigned to it in Rule 10.
Alteration in the registration certificate is subject to the prescribed fee and the amended registration framework.

Companies/firms must update prescribed registration particulars annually through the online mechanism, including changes to address, products and numbers manufactured/packed/imported in the previous year and country of origin, as specified by the 2026 amendment.
An incomplete application is returned to the applicant within the prescribed seven working days.
